{{short description|Russian historian (born 1973)}}
{{Notability|Bio|date=March 2021}}

'''Lyubov Vinogradova''' (born 1973) is a [[Russians|Russian]] [[historian]], researcher, translator and journalist.<ref name="FB">{{cite web |title=The best books on Books from the KGB Archives recommended by Lyubov Vinogradova |website=Five Books |date=9 May 2010 |accessdate=25 July 2026 |url=https://fivebooks.com/best-books/lyubov-vinogradova-on-books-from-the-kgb-archives/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190722033053/https://fivebooks.com/best-books/lyubov-vinogradova-on-books-from-the-kgb-archives/ |archive-date=22 July 2019 |url-status=live}}</ref>

== Biography ==
She was born in [[Moscow]] and graduated from the [[Moscow Agricultural Academy]], where she also obtained a PhD in [[microbiology]], followed by a second degree in English and German.<ref name="hachette">{{cite web|url=https://www.hachette.co.uk/contributor/lyuba-vinogradova/|title=Lyuba Vinogradova|website=Hachette UK|accessdate=2021-03-05}}</ref><ref name="FB" />

In 1994, while still preparing her doctorate, she became a [[research assistant]] for [[Antony Beevor]] in [[Volgograd]], helping him gain access to Soviet archival material and conducting research (including [[oral history]] interviews) for his [[magnum opus]] ''[[Stalingrad (Beevor book)|Stalingrad]]'' (1998).<ref>{{cite news |last=Glenny |first=Misha |author-link=Misha Glenny |title=Antony Beevor: Researching the Russian army gave me PTSD |work=[[The Times]] |date=14 May 2022 |accessdate=25 July 2026 |url=https://www.thetimes.com/life-style/article/antony-beevor-researching-the-russian-army-gave-me-ptsd-dcrgth89x}}</ref><ref name="hachette" /><ref name="JG">{{cite news |last=Glancy |first=Josh |title=With her, the lost ‘Night Witch’ war heroines are flying again |work=The Times |date=19 April 2015 |accessdate=25 July 2026 |url=https://www.thetimes.com/comment/register/article/with-her-the-lost-night-witch-war-heroines-are-flying-again-cqd6l07kjt8}}</ref> In 2005, she co-edited a volume of [[Vasily Grossman]]'s writings with Beevor.<ref name="AN">{{cite web|url=https://andrewnurnberg.com/book-author/lyuba-vinogradova/|title=Lyuba Vinogradova Archives |website=Andrew Nurnberg Associates International |accessdate=2021-03-05}}</ref> Their collaboration continued as late as 2026.<ref>{{citation |last=Beevor |first=Antony |title=Rasputin and the Downfall of the Romanovs |location=London |publisher=[[Weidenfeld & Nicolson]] |year=2026 |p= |isbn=9781399617628}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Christiansen |first=Rupert |title=The truth about Rasputin (and his vulgar way with women) |work=[[The Daily Telegraph]] |date=10 March 2026 |accessdate=25 July 2026 |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/books/non-fiction/rasputin-antony-beevor-review/}}</ref>

She has also worked for historians [[Simon Sebag Montefiore]] and [[Max Hastings]], helping them with Russian sources,<ref>{{cite news |title=The Secret War: Spies, Codes and Guerrillas, 1939–45 by Max Hastings |work=The Times |date=5 September 2015 |accessdate=25 July 2026 |url=https://www.thetimes.com/comment/register/article/the-secret-war-spies-codes-and-guerrillas-1939-45-by-max-hastings-b3kc079qt9f}}</ref><ref name="JG" /><ref name="AN" /> and acted as an editor for [[Jonathan Dimbleby]], to whom she supplied material on the [[Holodomor|Ukrainian famine of 1932–1933]].<ref>{{citation |last=Dimbleby |first=Jonathan |author-link=Jonathan Dimbleby |title=Russia: A Journey to the Heart of a Land and Its People |location=London |publisher=BBC Books |year=2008 |p=x |isbn=9780563539124 |url=https://archive.org/details/russiajourneytoh0000dimb_u6h4/}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Evans |first=Julian |title=Jonathan Dimbleby's Barbarossa captures the pitiless human cost of war |work=The Telegraph |date=17 April 2021 |accessdate=25 July 2026 |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/books/what-to-read/jonathan-dimblebys-barbarossa-captures-pitiless-human-cost-war/}}</ref>

Her own 2015 and 2017 English-language history books on [[Red Army]]'s female soldiers have been translated into Spanish and Polish.

She emigrated to the [[United Kingdom]] due to her family connection to [[Boris Nemtsov]], the former leader of the [[Union of Right Forces]] assassinated in 2015. She lives in [[Cardiff]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Blair |first=David |title=Antony Beevor: For Russia, conspicuous cruelty is a necessary weapon of war |work=The Telegraph |date=30 November 2025 |accessdate=25 July 2026 |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2025/11/30/antony-beevor-interview |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251130083933/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2025/11/30/antony-beevor-interview/ |archive-date=30 November 2025 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Works ==
* ''Defending the Motherland: The Soviet Women who Fought Hitler's Aces'', London: [[MacLehose Press]], 2015, {{ISBN|9780857051929}} (Spanish and Polish translations 2016)
* ''Avenging Angels: Soviet Women Snipers on the Eastern Front (1941–1945)'', London: MacLehose Press, 2017, {{ISBN|9780857051967}} (Spanish translation 2017, Polish translation 2018)
